headline: which bones is your bone age
the problem
body: bone age is read from a hand and wrist X-ray and then applied to the entire skeleton as if every growth plate is at the same point. | this is predicated on the narrow assumption that all plates share one clock. they dont, and the data on this is not subtle.
punch: the hand is not a proxy for the legs.

headline: dolan et al
body: in mice, *epiphyseal fusion* occurs at approximately **3 weeks** in phalanges and **4 weeks** in metacarpals but has not yet occurred at **12 weeks** in tibias or femurs. rats, same order: **12** and **16** weeks vs still open. | so the hand is done while the leg has barely started, in two species.
punch: _small bones first. long bones last. every time._

headline: and its not just timing
body: at one week the metacarpal was growing at **49%** of the tibial rate and *proliferation per column* was **46%**. every structural and functional marker of *growth plate senescence*, ie the plate exhausting its divisions, was more advanced in the metacarpals and phalanges. | the hand is not merely earlier. it is further along the same curve at every age.
punch: ==your hand bones run at half speed and age faster.==

headline: so, how
body: it doesnt. this leads us to the actually interesting result. *chondrocytes* isolated from phalanges proliferated slower than those from tibias, but adding IGF-1 to the phalangeal cells raised proliferation **to match untreated tibial cells**. | the cells are equivalent. the local IGF signalling is not. thats the entire difference.
punch: the bone is the same. the signal reaching it isnt.

headline: kvist 2021
body: in humans, MRI of wrist, knee and ankle in **958 subjects** aged 14 to 21. fusion timing varied by site within the same person and complete fusion occurred approximately **2 years earlier** in girls. | *pubertal stage* correlated with fusion at every site, **0.514 to 0.598** in males.

headline: and the part
body: the same study tested physical activity directly. no significant correlation in males at any site, one very low correlation at the female wrist (**0.095**), nothing else. **BMI** did correlate, 0.186 to 0.384. | there is a dominating, yet unjustified worship of training as the variable that spends your plates. in the largest imaging dataset on this, it barely registered.
punch: ==body composition tracked maturation. training did not.==

headline: so
subhead: what you do with the number
body: treat bone age as an estimate from your fastest ageing bones. track pubertal stage, since that is what actually correlated. and stop modelling your legs off your hand.
